notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

Evidence is asked as queries, bench_e :- E. and each query Q as bench_qe_Q :- Q, E., E the conjunction of what the program observes, so that P(Q | E) is P(bench_qe_Q) / P(bench_e); a probability in exponent notation is written out, the same double; and V is X is written V = X, as aspmc's grammar reads them. notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.

notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

# conjugate gaussians (Jordan 2010): a standard normal mean given two
# observed points, each normal around it with variance 1; the expectation
# of the mean (the paper's measure for a program that returns a number).
# Bit-blasting paper (Garg, Holtzen, Van den Broeck, Millstein, PLDI 2024),
# Table 2: 23 bits, 16 pieces. From Tractables/Alea.jl branch hybit
# (96b69a5, the paper's artifact) benchmarks/conjugate_gaussians/
# conjugate_gaussians.jl (Apache License 2.0), with Dice.jl's names
# changed to Alea's (Dice to Alea, @dice to @alea), and the observations 1
# and 2 rather than the file's 8 and 9: the expectations the artifact
# records for its runs (benchmarks/conjugate_gaussians/results.txt) are
# near 1, the posterior mean of 1 and 2 (17/3 is that of 8 and 9), and its
# ground truth for the table is 1.0 (benchmarks/plotting.ipynb). The 8 and
# 9 are the paper's Figure 5, data/alea/bitblast/conjugate_ex3.jl. The
# body is otherwise unchanged.
using Alea, Distributions

const QUERY = :expectation
const bits = 15
const pieces = 16
const DFiP = DistFix{8 + bits, bits}
const data = DFiP.([1.0, 2.0])
const add_arg = true

model() = @alea begin
    a = bitblast(DFiP, Normal(0, 1), pieces, -16.0, 16.0)
    for datapt in data
        gaussian_observe(DFiP, pieces, -16.0, 16.0, a, 1.0, datapt, add=add_arg, exp=false)
    end
    a
end

# Conjugate Gaussians with low-probability observations (bit-blasting
# paper, Garg, Holtzen, Van den Broeck, Millstein, PLDI 2024, Section 2.3,
# Figures 5 and 6): a standard normal mean and two observations, 8 and 9,
# each normal around it with variance 1; the posterior is normal with mean
# 17/3 and variance 1/3. The paper plots it at 16 bits after the binary
# point and 2048 pieces; here the program is queried for its expectation.
# From Tractables/Alea.jl hybrid/benchmarks/conjugate_gaussians/
# conjugate_gaussians.jl at cf5e5b8 (Apache License 2.0): the bits and
# pieces, read from the command line there, are constants, and the
# plotting and results file are dropped; the body is otherwise unchanged.
using Alea, Distributions

const QUERY = :expectation
const bits = 16
const pieces = 2048
const DFiP = DistFix{8 + bits, bits}
const data = DFiP.([8.0, 9.0])
const add_arg = true

model() = @alea begin
    a = bitblast(DFiP, Normal(0, 1), pieces, -16.0, 16.0)
    for datapt in data
        gaussian_observe(DFiP, pieces, -16.0, 16.0, a, 1.0, datapt, add=add_arg, exp=false)
    end
    a
end
